analysis.title: GS Quinn - Nasdaq Futures: Signs of Asset Manager Sponsorship?
key_insights: AI optimism pushed the Nasdaq index to new all-time highs. From September 29 to October 6 Nasdaq rose 2.9%, ahead of the S&P (+1.9%) and Russell 2000 (+0.8%).
GS's AI Leaders and Broad AI baskets rose 6.4% and 5.6% over the same week, helped by significant infrastructure agreements.

Nasdaq futures aggregate open interest rose considerably, which signals a potential dominance of long initiations. OI increased in 3 of the 5 sessions for a net $8.9bn, with the largest increases on October 2 and 5 alongside price strength.

Funding market changes point to simultaneous short selling. Nasdaq 3 month funding cheapened in outright terms and moved sideways relative to the S&P, so outright shorts and/or hedging conceivably drove some of the OI builds.
Sponsorship from the largest Non-Dealer cohort is questionable. Asset Manager gross longs have generally declined since reaching a nominal max on June 2.
The historically positive correlation between Asset Manager gross long changes (in contract terms) and price was nil as of the September 29 Commitment of Traders update.

sector_views.rationale: AI baskets are leading the Nasdaq to record highs, but asset manager buying is not confirming the move in the CFTC data.

risk_factors: Asset Manager gross longs have fallen since the June 2 peak, so the record highs lack confirmation from the largest Non-Dealer cohort.
Part of the open interest increase may reflect outright shorts or hedging rather than long initiations, based on funding market moves.
vol_and_positioning: Nasdaq futures aggregate open interest rose a net $8.9bn over the week, up in 3 of 5 sessions, with the largest increases on October 2 and 5 alongside price strength.

Asset Manager gross longs in Nasdaq futures have generally declined since a nominal max on June 2.
